answer.rationale: The current release carries a compliance-protected security patch, so rollback_release is unavailable; the incident is a 90-minute climb in write-path latency, not an abrupt availability collapse, so regional_failover would be an oversized move and route_read_replicas addresses read/dashboard load rather than heavy settlement writes; enable_circuit_breaker risks shedding customer writes and violates the stated objective. Proactively adding capacity has the best fit: it directly expands write-path headroom during peak settlement traffic while preserving all writes, and the closest durable precedent (memory_b3) indicates that provisioning headroom before load pressure kept queue depth flat. I am pulling memory_b3 because it is the only candidate direction supported by a directly analogous intervention, and the inherited summary alone does not confirm the provisioning scope, timing, or any caveats that would change whether a similar capacity intervention is safe and effective under concurrent security-patch constraints. If verification reveals that prior headroom provisioning succeeded only under different load characteristics or required long lead time, I would still prefer guarded capacity addition over the other available options, but would size it more conservatively and monitor closely.
